mcqs.question: A solid is formed by attaching a right circular cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm to the base of a right circular cone having the same base radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. Find the total surface area of the composite solid (the common circular face is not exposed).
mcqs.explanation: Surface area = curved area of cylinder + curved area of cone + bottom base of cylinder. Curved cylinder = 2πrh = 2π·3·10 = 60π. Curved cone = πrl where l = √(r²+h²) = √(3²+6²)=√45 = 3√5, so area = π·3·3√5 = 9π√5. Bottom base of cylinder = πr² = 9π. Total = 60π + 9π√5 + 9π = 69π + 9π√5 ≈ 279.98 cm², which matches option A.

mcqs.question: A toy consists of a rectangular block on which a solid hemisphere is placed perfectly on one of its faces. Which pair of standard solids correctly describes the components of this toy?
mcqs.explanation: The rectangular block is a rectangular prism (also called a cuboid). The rounded top part is a hemisphere, which is half of a sphere. Hence the correct pair is rectangular prism and hemisphere. The other options describe different shapes not present in the toy.

mcqs.question: A right circular cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 10 cm is attached to the base of a right circular cone of the same radius and height 12 cm. What is the total exposed surface area of the resulting solid?
mcqs.explanation: Exposed area = curved surface of cylinder (2πrh = 100π) + curved surface of cone (πrl, l = √(5²+12²)=13, so 65π) + bottom base of cylinder (πr² = 25π). The common circular face is hidden and must not be counted. Total = 100π + 65π + 25π = 190π cm². Option B incorrectly adds the area of the common face twice.

mcqs.question: A solid consists of a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 14 cm with a hemisphere of the same radius placed on its top. What is the total volume of the composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cylinder volume = πr²h = π·7²·14 = 686π cm³. Hemisphere volume = (2/3)πr³ = (2/3)π·7³ = (2/3)π·343 = 686/3 π cm³ ≈ 228.667π cm³. Total volume = (686 + 228.667)π = 914.667π cm³ ≈ 2875.6 cm³, which rounds to 2876 cm³ (option A).

mcqs.learning_point: Avoid counting hidden surfaces when finding exposed area
mcqs.question: A right circular cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm is attached to the base of a right circular cylinder of the same radius and height 6 cm. Which statement correctly describes the exposed surface area of the composite solid?

options.A: It equals the sum of the individual exposed areas minus the area of the common circular face.
options.B: It equals the sum of the total surface areas of the cone and the cylinder.
options.C: It includes the area of the common circular face twice.
options.D: It is only the curved surface area of the cylinder.

mcqs.answer: It equals the sum of the individual exposed areas minus the area of the common circular face.
mcqs.explanation: When two solids are joined, the face where they meet becomes internal and must be excluded from the exposed surface area. Therefore, the correct total exposed area is obtained by adding the exposed parts of each solid and subtracting the area of the common face. Options B, C, and D either count the hidden face or ignore parts of the surface.

mcqs.question: A water tank consists of a rectangular cuboid base measuring 10 m × 8 m × 2 m, surmounted by a hemispherical dome of radius 4 m. The base of the cuboid rests on the ground and is not painted. Find the total surface area that needs to be painted.
mcqs.explanation: Exposed area of cuboid = top (10×8 = 80 m²) + four side faces (2×10×2 + 2×8×2 = 40 + 32 = 72 m²) = 152 m². Hemispherical dome surface (excluding its circular base) = 2πr² = 2π·4² = 32π ≈ 100.53 m². Total painted area = 152 + 100.53 ≈ 252.53 m², which rounds to 253 m² (option A).

mcqs.question: Which of the following composite solids is made by joining a right circular cone and a right circular cylinder?

options.A: A solid formed by placing a cone on top of a cylinder of the same base radius
options.B: A solid formed by attaching a hemisphere to a cube
options.C: A solid formed by joining two pyramids at their bases
options.D: A solid formed by merging a sphere with a rectangular prism

mcqs.answer: A solid formed by placing a cone on top of a cylinder of the same base radius
mcqs.explanation: Option A explicitly describes a composite solid consisting of a cone and a cylinder sharing the same circular base. The other options involve different shapes (hemisphere, pyramids, sphere, prism) and do not match the description.

mcqs.question: A solid is formed by attaching a square pyramid of base side 5 cm and height 6 cm to one face of a cube of side 5 cm. What is the total exposed surface area of the composite solid?
mcqs.explanation: Cube SA = 6×5² = 150 cm². One face (25 cm²) is hidden, so exposed cube area = 150 – 25 = 125 cm². Pyramid base (25 cm²) is also hidden. Slant height l = √((2.5)² + 6²) = √42.25 = 6.5 cm. Area of one triangular face = ½×base×slant = ½×5×6.5 = 16.25 cm². Four such faces give 65 cm². Exposed pyramid area = 65 cm². Total exposed area = 125 + 65 = 190 cm², matching option A.
